meta.source: SEC EDGAR Form N-PORT (NPORT-P) portfolio holdings
meta.grain: one row per (filing, holding) where the holding is India exposure

definitions.india_listed: ISIN begins 'INE' — a genuinely INDIA-LISTED security. The strict test, and the one the headline numbers use.
definitions.india_exposure: any of: ISIN 'INE', issuer country 'IN', or currency 'INR'. Broader — it also catches ADRs and offshore India plays. Kept separate from india_listed on purpose.
definitions.val_usd: the filer's own reported USD value of the position.
definitions.pct_of_fund: the filer's own percent-of-net-assets. NOT recomputed here, so it stays consistent with the filing.
definitions.n_funds: how many of the SCANNED funds report that Indian security.

caveats: ★ N-PORT is filed MONTHLY but only the THIRD month of each fiscal quarter is made PUBLIC, so the public series is quarterly at best and consecutive public reports for one fund are ~3 months apart. Do not read it as a monthly series.
Filings appear ~60 days after the period end.

The fund universe is a CURATED, NAMED SAMPLE matched against the real quarterly index — India-dedicated and large EM/international complexes. It is NOT the whole US fund universe; `coverage.funds_scanned` lists who was included.
Ownership aggregates use LONG EQUITY (assetCat 'EC', payoffProfile not Short) only; shorts and derivatives are stored and flagged but excluded from them.
Fiscal quarters differ across funds, so one `period_end` bucket can mix funds whose reporting dates are weeks apart.
A fund holding no India at all is read and counted, but contributes no rows — so absence here means 'no India in that filing', not 'not scanned'.
